facts.text: Morris Heights is a residential neighborhood in the West Bronx, bounded by Burnside Avenue, Jerome Avenue, the Cross Bronx Expressway, and the Harlem River.
University Avenue runs through the heart of Morris Heights, serving as its main thoroughfare.
The arrival of the Harlem River Railroad in the 1840s and the construction of the High Bridge linked the Bronx to Manhattan, spurring early growth.
During the Great Depression and World War II, Morris Heights remained a stable community of factory workers, shopkeepers, and teachers.
The High Bridge, New York City’s oldest surviving bridge, was restored and reopened to pedestrians in 2015, reconnecting the Bronx with Manhattan.
Morris Heights is believed to be the birthplace of Hip Hop culture in the 1970s, a claim that highlights its cultural legacy.
